title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. G is a group (scheme) with determinant δ_G: G → G_m and kernel SG. There is a subgroup T_0 ⊂ G that δ_G maps isomorphically onto G_m, so G ≃ T_0·SG is a semidirect product. Earlier pages fixed quantities (152) and solved for unknowns (153) via the formulas (154). Given U ∈ ΓG one writes U = f^{-1}u with f ∈ ΓSG and u ∈ ΓT_0. This gives α = u a^{-1}, β = U b^{-1}, α_0 = f^{-1}α, β_0 = f^{-1}β (formulas numbered (157) on the previous page). Here a and b are fixed elements of the tori (or normalizers) T_ρ and T_σ, which are embedded in G by (155).

This page, part 1: determinant bookkeeping.
- det u = det U = μ.
- det α = det u · det(a)^{-1} = ε' (a sign), using (152').
- det β = det U · det(b)^{-1} = 1.
- Since f ∈ SG, det α_0 = det α = ε' and det β_0 = det β = 1.
- Hence α, α_0 ∈ G^{±1} := {g : (det g)^2 = 1} and β, β_0 ∈ SG.
Grothendieck flags a tacit hypothesis: the characters δ_ρ, δ_σ of (135) must be induced by δ_G through the embeddings (155).

Part 2: making the loop relation meaningful. The target relation (again numbered (157)) is
[α,ρ] = ε[β,σ] ε_1(μ−1).
This is the linearized analogue of the Galois/GT 'équation des lacets' x ↦ x^λ, with μ playing the role of the cyclotomic character λ. For it to make sense one needs:
- sections ρ, σ of G, more precisely of T_ρ and T_σ (or their normalizers);
- a strict unipotent one-parameter subgroup ε_1: G_a → SG, evaluated at μ−1.

Part 3: substitution. Substitute α = u a^{-1}. Since a and ρ commute in the commutative torus T_ρ, [u a^{-1}, ρ] = [u, ρ]. Do the same with β = U b^{-1}. Then b need not commute with σ (it may only lie in the normalizer), so a residual factor b^{-1}σ(b) remains:
(*) [u,ρ] = ε U (b^{-1}σ(b))^{±1} σ(U)^{-1} ε_1(μ−1).
The next page turns this into conditions:
- (158a) b^{-1}σ(b) = ε_σ(b);
- (158b) ρ(u) = ε_1(1−μ)σ(u) on T_0;
- (159) σ^{-1}ρ = ε_0 u_0, with T_0 acting on a unipotent group L_0 through the character det.
The typical model is G = GL_2 with T_0 = diag(t,1) and L_0 the upper unipotent group, where conjugation multiplies by t = det.

Purpose: build explicit linear-algebraic-group models (GL_2/Borel-type) in which the loop equations defining the Galois/GT action on π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) can be written and solved, with det standing in for the cyclotomic character.
errors: Equation number (157) is used twice: on the previous page for the formulas α = u a^{-1}, etc., and here for the relation [α,ρ] = ε[β,σ]ε_1(μ−1).

The determinant computation is consistent only under the tacit hypothesis, which Grothendieck himself flags, that δ_ρ and δ_σ are restrictions of δ_G. The value ε' depends on (152'), which is not visible here.

In (*) the exponent/sign on the factor (b^{-1}σ(b)) is hard to read and possibly inconsistent: a direct expansion of [U b^{-1}, σ] gives U b^{-1} σ b U^{-1} σ^{-1}. The next page writes the condition as b^{-1}σ(b) = ε_σ(b). Grothendieck himself writes 'attention aux signes' (watch the signs) on the next page.

ideas.what: Determinant bookkeeping showing the solution elements α, α_0 lie in G^{±1} = {(det g)^2 = 1} and β, β_0 lie in SG, given a splitting G = T_0 ⋉ SG with T_0 ≅ G_m via det.
ideas.modern_name: semidirect decomposition GL_n = G_m ⋉ SL_n; det as a stand-in for the cyclotomic character

ideas.what: A linear-group model of the 'loop equation' [α,ρ] = ε[β,σ]ε_1(μ−1): commutators with torus elements ρ, σ, corrected by a unipotent one-parameter subgroup evaluated at μ−1. This is the analogue of x ↦ x^λ in the GT/Galois action on π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}), with μ = det the analogue of the cyclotomic character.
ideas.modern_name: linear/metabelian (Burau-type, GL_2-Borel) representations of the Galois/GT action; cf. Ihara's universal power series for Jacobi sums
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1985–86) for metabelian/linear representations of the Galois action on pro-ℓ π_1; Drinfeld/Ihara for GT
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Galois action on π_1 of P^1 minus 3 points but not these explicit linear models; unsure for La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Using commutativity of a torus T_ρ to cancel a ∈ T_ρ in [u a^{-1}, ρ] = [u, ρ]. When b lies only in the normalizer of T_σ, a correction term b^{-1}σ(b) appears and is later forced to be a unipotent ε_σ(b).

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks explicit solutions of the loop equations inside a linear algebraic group G with determinant (a GL_2/Borel-type model). The determinant plays the cyclotomic character, and a torus acts on a unipotent L_0 through det. On the next page he calls the resulting condition ad hoc and wants 'more convincing' formulations. Systematically classifying such linear models of GT/loop-equation solutions does not seem to have been taken up in exactly this form, although Ihara's metabelian representations cover related ground.
missed.quote: il faut se donner des sections ρ, σ de G (ou plus précisément des sections de T_ρ et de T_σ ...), et un unipotent strict ε_1 ∈ ΓSG, pour que la relation (157) prenne un sens.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of modest interest as a source for low-dimensional linear representations of GT-type actions. It is likely subsumed by Ihara's power-series and metabelian results, so novelty is probably limited.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly routine determinant bookkeeping and commutator manipulation. Its interest lies only in documenting that Grothendieck tested the loop equations in explicit linear-group models with det as cyclotomic character, a theme parallel to Ihara's later work, but with nothing finished or striking here.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the struck-out symbol before '= det u' is illegible, and the next symbol is the double-underlined U, i.e. 'det u = det U = μ'.
'O'iquatsion [?]' is likely the end of the phrase 'Pour parvenir à la relation non ... d'équation' or similar. The relation is labelled (157) and the braces name ξ = [α,ρ] and η = [β,σ].
'(ou plus précisément dans dans [?], de T_ρ et de T_σ' should read '(ou plus précisément des sections, resp.t, de T_ρ et de T_σ (ou leurs normalisateurs))'.

The parenthetical after 'utilisant la commutativité de T_ρ' should read roughly '(ce qui ne suffirait pas pour normalisateurs de T_ρ, ce qu'on ne fait nécessairement pas ici)'. It is only partly legible; the transcribed '[?] suffisait par [?] normaux' is wrong.
In (*) the second factor is β's U (double-underlined), and the middle factor reads (b^{-1}σ(b))^{-1} or similar, with uncertain exponent.
